title: Decode XORed Permutation
statement:
Some array `perm` contains each of the integers `1, 2, ..., n` exactly once, and `n` is odd. You only see `encoded`, which has `n - 1` entries, where `encoded[i]` equals `perm[i] XOR perm[i + 1]` (bitwise exclusive or). For instance, `perm = [2, 3, 1]` would give `encoded = [1, 2]`.

Reconstruct and return `perm`. The input is guaranteed to come from exactly one such permutation.
notes:
## Intuition

If we knew `perm[0]`, every later value would follow, because `perm[i + 1] = perm[i] XOR encoded[i]`. A brute force could try all `n` first values and keep the one that yields a permutation, costing O(n²). XOR gives the first value directly. The XOR of all of `1..n` is the XOR of every element of `perm`. Because `n` is odd, the entries `encoded[1], encoded[3], ...` cover `perm[1] XOR perm[2]`, `perm[3] XOR perm[4]`, and so on, which is every element except `perm[0]`. XORing the two totals cancels everything except `perm[0]`.

## Approach

1. Let `n = encoded.length + 1` and `allValues = 1 XOR 2 XOR ... XOR n`.
2. XOR together the odd-indexed entries of `encoded` to get `allButFirst`, the XOR of `perm[1..n-1]`.
3. Set `perm[0] = allValues XOR allButFirst`.
4. Walk forward: `perm[i + 1] = perm[i] XOR encoded[i]`, then return `perm`.

## Example 1, step by step

`encoded = [3, 1]`, so `n = 3` and `allValues = 1 XOR 2 XOR 3 = 0`. The only odd index is 1, so `allButFirst = encoded[1] = 1`. Then `perm[0] = 0 XOR 1 = 1`, `perm[1] = 1 XOR 3 = 2` and `perm[2] = 2 XOR 1 = 3`, giving `[1, 2, 3]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): three linear passes.
- Space: O(n) for the returned array, O(1) extra.

## Pitfalls

- Use the odd indices of `encoded` (1, 3, 5, ...), not the even ones; the even ones would include `perm[0]` and miss the last element.
- XOR `1..n` with `n = encoded.length + 1`, not `encoded.length`.
- The trick depends on `n` being odd so that the odd-indexed pairs cover `perm[1..n-1]` exactly.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of the hidden permutation |
| `allValues` | XOR of every integer from 1 to n |
| `allButFirst` | XOR of `perm[1]` through `perm[n-1]` |
| `perm` | the rebuilt permutation |
| `i` | position in `encoded` |

narration.4: Accumulate the XOR of 1 through n...
